description.value: This preliminary study examined brain responses to food cues in obese adults with evening hyperphagia compared with obese adults without evening hyperphagia, before and after a mid-day meal, using functional magnetic resonance imaging.

spans.text: This preliminary study examined the brain response to food cues using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) in seven obese adults with EH compared to seven obese adults without EH.

value: we hypothesized that obese persons with EH compared to matched controls would show significantly different brain activation in response to food images in prefrontal and limbic regions.

spans.text: Based on studies showing reduced daytime hunger and food intake in persons with EH compared to weight-matched controls ( ), we hypothesized that obese persons with EH compared to matched controls would show significantly different brain activation in response to food images in prefrontal and limbic regions.

description.value: Seven obese adults meeting criteria for evening hyperphagia and seven matched control participants were studied before and immediately after eating a standardized small meal.

spans.text: Seven obese adults meeting criteria for EH (mean BMI = 37.9 kg/m 2 , mean age = 33.6 years, 6 female, 5 Caucasian) and seven control participants matched for BMI, age, gender, ethnicity, and education level, were selected on the basis of baseline eating patterns and demographic characteristics from a cohort of 80 obese adults enrolled in a study examining the neural predictors of weight loss.
